dataflow.summary: Valid suspended-admin JWT -> app_metadata role check -> service-role user update

reachability.summary: Directly reachable while the suspended administrator session remains valid.

attackPath.summary: Suspended admin reuses a valid bearer token to call privileged APIs and direct RLS-protected operations.

confidence.rationale: Direct source review shows is_admin reads only app metadata and admin-update-user-role omits the suspension check used by a sibling privileged function.

findings.remediation: Make the central authorization check require an unsuspended profile and agreement between profile and signed metadata roles. Apply it consistently to every admin RLS policy and privileged Edge Function; revoke sessions when suspending an account.

rootCause.summary: Administrative authorization is derived from role metadata without consulting the account suspension state.

severity.rationale: A constrained attacker who previously held admin access can create durable replacement admins and continue accessing admin-protected data after suspension.

findings.summary: The central admin authorization helper and role-management endpoint trust signed role metadata without enforcing profiles.is_suspended, allowing a suspended admin with a live session to retain database and role-management privileges.
findings.title: Suspended administrators retain broad privileged access

counterEvidence: send-contact-reply correctly checks is_suspended, demonstrating the intended control, but that check is not centralized.
validation.summary: The same suspended identity remains accepted by is_admin-backed RLS and can reach auth.admin.updateUserById through the role endpoint.

dataflow.summary: Public anon key -> donations SELECT -> USING (true) -> PII response

attackPath.summary: Anonymous PostgREST SELECT returns donor rows.

confidence.rationale: The effective migration sequence explicitly grants anon SELECT USING (true), and later hardening changes only INSERT.

findings.remediation: Drop donations_select_public. Allow SELECT only to authenticated administrators through a suspension-aware admin check; expose only de-identified aggregates through a separate narrow view if public totals are needed.

rootCause.summary: A permissive public SELECT policy was introduced for an operational table containing donor PII and never removed.

severity.rationale: Unauthenticated, low-complexity enumeration exposes sensitive donor PII and financial relationships across all records.

findings.summary: An unconditional anon SELECT policy exposes names, emails, phones, organizations, donation amounts, frequency, status, and messages through PostgREST.
findings.title: Anonymous users can read all donor records and financial metadata

validation.summary: PostgreSQL permissive policies are OR-combined, so the admin-read policy cannot narrow the unconditional public policy.

dataflow.summary: Public anon key -> partners SELECT -> USING (true) -> inquiry response

attackPath.summary: Anonymous PostgREST SELECT returns partnership submissions.

confidence.rationale: The schema and unconditional anon SELECT policy directly establish exposure.

findings.remediation: Separate submitted inquiries from approved public partner profiles. Remove public SELECT from the inquiry table and expose only reviewed publication fields from a dedicated table or filtered view.

rootCause.summary: Public partner profiles and private partnership submissions share one table protected by an unconditional public SELECT policy.

severity.rationale: Unauthenticated bulk disclosure exposes business contact information and private proposal content.

findings.summary: The partners table mixes public presentation data with private inquiry names, emails, organizations, interests, and messages, then exposes every row publicly.
findings.title: Anonymous users can read all partnership inquiries

validation.summary: No later migration removes or filters partners_select_public.

dataflow.summary: Anonymous JSON -> service-role contact insert -> admin query -> notification fan-out

attackPath.summary: Automated POSTs create contacts and admin notifications.

confidence.rationale: The source contains no application-level abuse control before either privileged write.

findings.remediation: Add edge rate limits, bot challenges, burst/deduplication controls, and monitoring before service-role work. Revoke direct public table INSERT and funnel submissions through the controlled endpoint; aggregate admin notifications.

rootCause.summary: Anonymous intake is unmetered and privileged writes amplify each request; direct public INSERT also bypasses any future function-only control.

severity.rationale: Low-complexity automation can consume storage and make the administrator inbox unusable.

findings.summary: Every unauthenticated request can create a service-role contact row and one attacker-controlled notification per active administrator without rate limiting, bot proof, or deduplication.
findings.title: Public contact intake permits unbounded database and notification amplification

validation.summary: Basic field limits bound each row but do not bound request count or fan-out.

dataflow.summary: Anonymous JSON -> service-role donation insert -> Paystack secret-backed initialization

attackPath.summary: Automated donation POSTs create rows and initialize Paystack transactions.

confidence.rationale: The service-role insert and Paystack call are directly reachable with no rate, challenge, quota, or idempotency control.

findings.remediation: Apply edge rate limits and bot proof before insertion, use idempotency keys and pending-row expiry, monitor provider volume, revoke redundant direct public donation INSERT, and implement signed server-side Paystack reconciliation.

rootCause.summary: A public request triggers privileged persistence and a paid external-provider operation without abuse controls or idempotency.

severity.rationale: Automation consumes database, function, provider, and operational capacity without compromising payment completion integrity.

findings.summary: Anonymous callers can create unlimited pending donation records and Paystack transaction initializations; failed or abandoned initializations retain records.
findings.title: Donation initialization is an unmetered database and payment-provider operation

validation.summary: Per-request amount and field validation do not restrict request volume; no completion webhook or pending-record expiry was found.

dataflow.outcome: Unauthorized submission, flooding, and status disclosure
dataflow.summary: Unauthenticated request -> optional auth fallthrough -> service-role duplicate query/insert

reachability.summary: Directly reachable without using the guarded UI.

attackPath.summary: Direct public invocation bypasses signup and probes or creates applications.

confidence.rationale: Invalid authentication explicitly falls through to userId=null and the duplicate response embeds existing.status.

findings.remediation: Require and validate a user bearer token, derive applicant identity and email from that user/profile, return a generic duplicate response without status, add rate limits and bot controls, and replace permissive direct INSERT policies with authenticated owner-only policies.

rootCause.summary: The account requirement exists only in client routing; the privileged backend treats authentication as optional and returns distinguishable private duplicate state.

severity.rationale: The public path defeats the intended registration control, supports review-workflow flooding, and leaks limited applicant state to an attacker who knows an email and public program ID.

findings.summary: The UI requires signup, but the service-role endpoint accepts missing or invalid authentication, creates two rows per application, and reveals whether a supplied email/program pair exists plus its workflow status.
findings.title: Public application endpoint bypasses the account requirement and leaks application status

validation.summary: A direct caller bypasses React routing; duplicate checks and inserts use service-role authority.

dataflow.summary: Victim email -> public endpoint -> service-role insert/update is_active=true

reachability.summary: No authentication or mailbox proof is required.

attackPath.summary: Anonymous caller submits a victim email and the service-role client activates it.

confidence.rationale: The endpoint sets is_active=true based solely on a syntactically valid email string.

findings.remediation: Implement confirmed opt-in with single-use expiring tokens. Store new requests as pending and never reactivate an unsubscribed address without fresh mailbox confirmation; add rate limiting and non-enumerating responses.

rootCause.summary: Subscription activation does not require a single-use confirmation proving control of the target mailbox.

severity.rationale: The issue corrupts consent state and enables list pollution; no active campaign sender was established in repository source.

findings.summary: Any anonymous caller who supplies another person's email can create an active subscription or reverse an inactive state without proving mailbox control.
findings.title: Newsletter endpoint can reactivate unsubscribed addresses without consent

validation.summary: Possession of the email string is the only requirement for initial activation or reactivation.
